mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 2% for three months signals a monetary policy tightening aimed at curbing inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL > 2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which reduces corporate revenues and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for six consecutive months AND UNRATE stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS is above its 12-month MA for six months and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals a supply-side recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA for eight consecutive months.
